Q1: What should this re-issue change, given that the silent pass no longer reproduces on `main`?
Choices:
A) Make pushes match commits (RECOMMENDED): when a push uses an unresolved or appended `GIT_DIR+=` / `GIT_WORK_TREE+=` override, never check the session checkout's PR history. Always ask instead. Also correct the "never applied" comment, update `test_appended_git_override_falls_back_without_using_rhs`, and change both hook copies (template and live `.claude/`) so they stay byte-identical.
B) Change no behaviour: add a regression test showing the #6305 exploit command asks or blocks on `main`, correct the misleading comment, and close the finding as fixed by #6509.
C) Try to resolve the effective override: when the appended value is an absolute path and the hook's own environment has no `GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE`, check the PR history of the repository that path names. Otherwise use option A.
**Note:** option C relies on the hook's environment matching the Bash tool's shell environment, which the hook cannot verify. That conflicts with the repository's fail-closed rule, so a planner may push it back to option A.
